done: A test kernel given as Image.gz was chosen by the bootloader, counted down, and could not start - the try was lost before the kernel logged a line, and looked like 'the bootloader ignores the entry'. devlab kernel install now refuses anything that is not an EFI executable and names the right file.
rejected: Acting on any of them before the bootloader's own record (the entry's try counter) was read.
title: Only an EFI program is offered to the bootloader

done: The kernel guard and the listening word, each from a mistake made today; two more steps recorded: a room of digital silence, and a try that reports its own outcome.
title: Two refusals, and what they cost to learn

considered: Leaving the microphone un-named as the safeguard.
done: A listening test now needs the explicit word that the microphone is placed, and refuses with the procedure otherwise - so the lesson of the worn microphone rests on the tool, not on memory.
rejected: That: a renamed file is a trick only its author remembers.
title: The word first

done: The landing is now the whole chain of Linux Phones on one page; the idea as the project wrote it follows; the phone in the lab has its own essence page.
rejected: Opening with a table of features a newcomer cannot yet place.
title: The lens opens with the essence

considered: Leaving the order to the data's ids.
done: Each table view says what its rows are (Feature, Part) and the features view lists its categories in a person's order - calls and messages first; the row names translated here.
rejected: That: alphabetical ids put 'power' first.
title: The lens names its rows and orders its groups

considered: Translating the family's data here.
done: The Linux Phones grand view declared as data (its family, eight views); its own text translated into Russian in its own translations table, marked by machine.
rejected: That: each project translates its own data; a lens only its own text.
title: The first lens, and its own Russian

considered: Keeping flash.sh as a fallback.
done: surya flashed from the pristine stock image by devlab flash and brought back by devlab provision, all 20 checks passing; flash.sh removed, as planned once devlab had done a real flash. A new check, root-fills-its-partition: the first boot had left the system at 2 GB on a 104 GB partition.
rejected: That: two ways to flash drift apart; the shell original stays in git history.
title: Flashed by devlab; the shell flash script retired

considered: Calling the 5 dB a fault.
done: With the author's EarPods as the lab's microphone, devlab hear played a 1000 Hz tone on each speaker and heard both: left at -24.0 dBFS, right at -29.2 dBFS, each over 70 dB above the silent room. The tones are in the manifest. Observed, not judged: the right read 5 dB quieter - the microphone's place or the speakers themselves; one measurement cannot say. WITHDRAWN the same day: the microphone was worn by the author and moved; neither the levels nor the 5 dB difference can be relied on.
rejected: That, on one measurement from one position.
title: Both speakers heard - then withdrawn

done: What this lab is - one particular phone, everything true of it written down, experiments that fall back by themselves - as a piece of writing for a reader who knows nothing of it.
rejected: A list of files.
title: The lab's idea, told for anyone

considered: A hand-made change the manifest lacked; a first-boot effect; the sensor proxy; a stream left open.
done: After the flash the audio DSP died on every suspend attempt (the attempts abort at once: the USB link cannot go idle). Found by experiment, one change at a time: not a first-boot effect (9 of 9 on the second boot), not the sensor proxy (15 of 15 without it), but hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper - 0 of 8 without it, and 0 of 9 on a clean boot with it masked, all 21 checks passing. Masked in the manifest, so every flash has it. The check's resume counter, which always said 0, rewritten in awk and checked against a boot with 24.
rejected: All four, each by its own measurement. The old 'rare' crash was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down.
title: The suspend crash found: a FastRPC helper attached at suspend

considered: Keeping the results with a caveat.
done: The microphone was the author's earphones, worn on his head: its distance from the phone changed as he moved. The levels measured, the difference seen between the two speakers, and the passes themselves cannot be relied on. The heard checks are out of the baseline and the lab's microphone is un-named until one is fixed in place; the tool stays, proven to work mechanically.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence, and a later failure would have looked like the phone getting worse.
title: What the ear heard is withdrawn

considered: Changing the shell's suspend hook.
done: Reported by the author: the phone kept reconnecting on his PC (26 USB disconnects in 5 minutes on the lab machine). On USB a suspend cannot complete, and the shell retried every 12 seconds, each attempt dropping the link. A small service holds a kernel wake lock while the port is connected to a host - independent of any shell - baked in by the manifest, with a check. Known before, never written down: it is now.
rejected: That: a fix inside one shell does not hold under another, or under none.
title: The USB link no longer flaps

considered: Marking parts as working from a device node alone.
done: Eight of the phone's twenty parts stood as unknown. The checks now also ask: is Wi-Fi joined and does the gateway answer; is Bluetooth powered and does it hear anything; is there a SIM and is the modem ready; does the kernel expose a headset-jack detector, a fingerprint reader, any motion or light sensor, any image sensor behind the camera pipeline. All read-only.
rejected: That: there and set up is what a machine can prove; the rest are witnessed tests.
title: More of the phone, measured

considered: Seven ports against the vendor's five as the cause.
done: The TX bus's port layout and timings match mainline sm8250 and the vendor's layout for the ports in use - not the cause. A boot to dump the SoundWire registers found this kernel has no SoundWire debugfs.
rejected: That, after comparing the ports actually used. And booting before checking the tool exists - a lesson: check the instrument first.
title: The port table cleared; a boot spent on a missing tool

considered: Describing the sensors from the models reported for this phone elsewhere.
done: Read from the phone and from sources, changing nothing: the camera pipeline and its control buses work; the phone's description lists no sensor. The vendor's kernel yields the wiring of seven sensor slots but no model names. Written up with the wiring table and a four-step way in (research/cameras.md).
rejected: That: hearsay. A chip should say what it is, on its own bus, before a driver is bound to it.
title: Why the cameras are dark, and the way in

considered: The macros' autosuspend; the upstream revert (it gives no reason).
done: Traced the codec's timeout to a bus clash on the microphone-side SoundWire bus, and that to one pin muxed to the wrong function in the audio pin driver (and one more on the receive side), read against the phone's own Android kernel. Corrected and rebuilt: the codec initialises and the sound card is made with it. Recording through it is next.
rejected: Guessing at clock fixes.
title: The microphone codec comes up

considered: Theories about the bootloader.
done: Booted the microphone test kernel (after finding the earlier tries had been given a gzip kernel): for the first time everything up to the codec came up; the card fails on one timeout. Measured which speaker is the bottom one. Saw a boot with no sound card and recorded it.
rejected: Acting before reading the bootloader's own record.
title: The microphone's chain, nearly whole

considered: A missing directory.
done: The SIM is seen and ready (1&1). The modem stays shutting-down and refuses to go online, even after a reboot; it loops on one file through tqftpserv, ending each read itself. One theory - a missing read-write directory - was checked and is wrong: the directory exists.
rejected: That: the program's own paths showed it exists.
title: The modem with a SIM

considered: Pasting the table change into the branch.
done: Listed the codec's recording side in the test kernel and read how the phone's own Android build routes its main microphone; the names match closely. Found that the kernel branch's pin driver differs from the tested tree - the fix is to be ported, not pasted.
rejected: That: the branch's driver is not the one that was tested.
title: The map to a first recording

considered: Keeping the bus awake.
done: The main-microphone route from the phone's Android build sets cleanly in the test kernel; the capture stream fails when it starts - the TX bus loses the codec exactly when it is reshaped for the stream. Ruled out power management. Measured the audio processor's once-a-second handover signal.
rejected: That as the answer: it changed nothing.
title: Two recording tries

done: The mark, the gatherer's caller and a place for this project's own records, written by ocoeco init.
title: Joined the Open Commons Observatory

considered: Using the observatory's repository as OCO's place (it holds the first observatory's own records, and is untouched until the author's observatory stands).
done: Made as a constellation by ocoeco init --gathers: it gathers ocoeco, ocoeco-engine, tad and lab-agent (oco-agent). Its mark says what it is and what it gathers; standing here the fulldome shows OCO.
title: OCO has a place of its own

considered: How we work as one roof - a separate working set beside the projects.
done: From the author: how a project works belongs to the project, like its backlog and milestones, tied to its goals - not a toolbox floating beside it; and its idea must be told by itself, for anyone. Specified as two standard tables and a chain: idea, path, workings, work.
rejected: That as the centre: shared tools are projects that others' workings name; the observatory follows the same four as everyone.
title: A project, whole

considered: An exception for protected repositories; loosening argenv's protection.
done: Found through argenv's protected branch: the gatherer wrote to the default branch and counted its own commits as activity. Gathered data now goes to an oco-data branch (the mark names it with path@branch), and activity leaves out commits by bots and workflows.
rejected: Both: one rule for every repository, and no project bends its protection for a tool.
title: Automation is not work

considered: Filling every step with something.
done: Its workings: what delivers and proves each step of its path, and why we care. Steps that nothing serves yet are left empty, to be seen.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves is a wish, and should show.
title: It tells its essence

considered: Terse cards of concepts.
done: The idea of ocoeco written as an ordered piece of writing in its own data - what it is, what it is for, a picture, its honest limit, where it stands - for a reader who knows nothing of it; shown by the observatory as an article.
rejected: Those as the idea: they name the parts for an insider.
title: Its idea, told for anyone

considered: A template repository.
done: ocoeco init and ocoeco check, with the specification's section 10: what had been done by hand for fifteen repositories is now the tool's job.
rejected: That: a template is copied once and drifts; a command writes what is current and never overwrites.
title: Joining in one command

considered: Retrying the raw file server; translated columns inside source tables.
done: ocoeco gather (activity, releases, CI) and its reusable workflow, running in all eleven marked repositories; shared tables read through GitHub's API; the lens kind and lens.toml in the harvest; the specification grown to lenses (8) and languages (9), with the rule that a project translates its own data.
rejected: The raw file server (stale for minutes, 501 to empty files); API headers sent to raw files; anyone translating another project's data.
title: Gatherers everywhere, lenses and languages

considered: Keeping the machinery in the observatory's engine; renaming tad-engine to ocoeco in place.
done: The repository and its principle (data made by work, never by hand); SPEC.md version 1 (the tad format at both levels, the mark, the standard tables, propagation, chaining, gatherers); the mark, discovery and the harvest moved in as the ocoeco crate and command, which the observatory now gathers with.
rejected: Both: the machinery belongs to the ecosystem, apart from the face; tad-engine keeps its history and stays frozen, tad lives on as the format's name.
title: ocoeco founded: the principle, the specification, the core

considered: Failing the check on a gap.
done: Before anything is published a project now learns how completely it tells its essence and what is still to tell - an idea with no limit, a step nothing delivers, a working that serves a step it does not have.
rejected: That: a gap is the truth about the project, not an error in its data.
title: check reads a repository's essence

done: Proposed by the author in the morning, live by noon: recorded by ocoeco hand, shown by the observatory, carried by land on every change. Its first run caught a pipe that swallowed a failure; fixed so a failure to record stops the landing.
title: Hand-work saturation, alive

done: ocoeco's 12 shared tables moved from Rust constants into language.toml, a tad declaration; a test compared the two table by table before the constants went; ocoeco note now checks rows with tad 0.4.0's check_row; 37 tests pass unchanged. A scan of all 22 projects: 20 conform; two use statement where the language says summary.
title: The shared language, declared as data

done: ocoeco note: one row added or updated, checked against the format. Its first use refused - ocoeco exported no decisions - so ocoeco now has its concepts and decisions, written with the tool.
title: Recording as a tool

done: land starts the observatory's harvest after merging a marked project; the harvest coalesces bursts. Triggering it by hand - 19 times - is over.
title: The picture follows every landing

considered: The problems lens before the first lens (decided after: it is better built as a real lens). Constellations before lenses (decided after: the mark's parent and kind are read in about eighty places, sixty of them in the hand-written views lenses replace). Embedding argenv now (recorded as its own step).
done: Declared the relations (thirteen; every link in 22 stars leads somewhere, 17 mended, 7 of them the tool's own). Named the acts glimpse, observe and focus, and the places star, constellation and observatory, with the fulldome as the outermost lens (decisions 2026-11-12-places-lenses-acts, -the-acts-named, -a-lens-has-a-glimpse, -a-lens-focuses, -names-of-places). Moved the shared language into six lenses, proven unchanged (-lenses-hold-the-language). Gave the work lens both faces: its focus as data, equal to the hand-written board byte for byte, which was then removed (-a-focus-is-data); and its glimpse, entries declared with what the computer supplies (-entries-declared). Gave every lens its entries.
rejected: pulse for record; show and showing for a lens's second face; a language for layout or conditions before a lens needs one; one file of tables written from outside.
title: OCO designed: places, lenses, acts - and the first lens made whole

considered: A fifth tab beside the others.
done: Named and asked for by the author: the chain seen, not read. A project lands on one page - the opening of its idea, its path, each step with what delivers and proves it (or nothing yet), and what is happening now - a flow of four numbered steps; four marks say how completely it tells its essence. A lens may show the same for its subject.
rejected: That: it is the landing; the other tabs are detail behind it.
title: Essence, the signature view

done: The view kinds ideas and log drawn (they were declared, not built); a lens with no candidates to compare shows its path and what its work says, with no empty comparison sections - needed by the Mnemonic Vocabulary lens, a project still at the idea stage.
rejected: Showing empty tables.
title: Lenses of ideas

considered: Filling every step with something.
done: Its idea written for anyone, and its workings: what delivers and proves each step of its path, and why we care. Steps that nothing serves yet are left empty, to be seen.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves is a wish, and should show.
title: It tells its essence

considered: Leaving red for open backlog items.
done: Seen on a project at the idea stage: every planned item showed the red sign of broken things. Planned work not yet started now has its own calm sign (an empty circle, grey) and a not-started milestone a grey ring; red stays for what is really broken or missing.
rejected: That: it painted an idea as a failure.
title: Not yet is not failure

considered: Requiring a project prefix on every criterion.
done: A milestone's criteria are read in its own project first, then anywhere - needed once a path (Rhizoid's) read another project's backlog on purpose; lenses the observatory finds but does not curate are shown under their own heading.
rejected: That: own-first reads naturally, and chaining stays one word.
title: Criteria in their own project; discovered lenses

considered: A bolder dot.
done: Looking at screenshots of the Russian pages: unknown cells read as blank (the faint dot is now a clear ?); the table's first column was named from a table name (the lens names its rows); categories came in an arbitrary order (the lens orders its groups, by the source category so it holds in every language); the milestone cards' chips were English (now messages). A second look showed the question marks white on pale: the table's "cell text is white" rule outranked the pale cells' own - the real cause of the invisible sign; their rule now outranks it, with a test.
rejected: That: a question mark says unknown without a legend.
title: Four things only eyes found

considered: Depending on ocoeco's code; restructuring every formatting call for messages; translating rendered pages.
done: The site, the path, a page per project, made by work, grand views drawn from lenses, one site per language with Fluent catalogs, each project's own data translations; the mark, discovery and harvest moved out to ocoeco; renamed ocoeco-engine.
rejected: Hard-coded grand views; unknown counted as failure; readiness from any done milestone; a lens translating other projects' data.
title: From a first site to ocoeco's rendering engine

considered: Reordering and rewording the cards.
done: Said by the author: the Idea tab told a commoner nothing - terse cards, alphabetical, written about a project rather than by it. A project's idea is now an ordered piece of writing in its own data, shown as an article; a lens opens with the idea of what it is about.
rejected: That: cards name the parts for an insider; an idea is read from the start by someone who knows nothing.
title: The idea, as an article

considered: A longer cut; a smaller font.
done: The path's labels ran into each other (reported with a screenshot): the path is now page layout - a cell per stop, labels shown whole and wrapping inside their own cell, scrolling sideways when narrow - with a test that forbids words inside SVG.
rejected: Both: they hide the fault until the next longer title or language.
title: Words never overlap

considered: Leaving the misleading commit as it is.
done: A commit claimed the word badge said what each word was chosen over; the edit had not matched the code, and the job only printed a count of zero. Fixed for real, and every edit in a job now stops the job when it does not take.
rejected: Hiding it: this entry and the correcting commit say so.
title: A check that only prints is not a check

considered: Fixing only the doubled count.
done: Found by looking at the front page: a doubled count on the grand cards, and behind it sentences in English written into the code. Both fixed; a test holds the card to one count and to words from the catalog.
rejected: That: the cause was words outside the catalog.
title: The cards speak the reader's language

done: Seen by looking at the Russian phone page: a count read '1 of 6', and each working's kind - tool, check, test - stayed English. The count is a plain fraction now and the kinds are words from the catalog.
rejected: Leaving small labels untranslated as 'technical'.
title: The last English words on a Russian page

considered: A separate page for the measure.
done: The four marks were computed inside one page; they are now one function, used by the Essence page, by every project's card on the front page, and by a single count of how many projects tell their whole essence - the same rule ocoeco check applies at home.
rejected: That: it belongs where the projects are listed.
title: The whole picture of essence, at a glance

considered: A store per project; ending the first milestone before graft; text as the content with structure as its index; starting at the kernel.
done: In one long conversation the author's idea was worked into its vocabulary (rhizome, node, shoot, conjure, graft), the manifesto was written, and Hypha's roadmap was drawn and redrawn until graft stood in the first milestone, the store was one per machine, and the graph - not text - was the source of truth.
rejected: All four - each corrected by the author in that conversation.
title: The idea, its name, and Hypha's roadmap

considered: Moving Rhizoid's repositories here at once.
done: The author's manifesto, and the concepts, decisions (with what was rejected), roadmap and path drawn from it and from the conversation, kept the ocoeco way in the author's new organization, with a lens curated in the observatory. On the periphery by the author's choice: recorded whole, not being built yet. Read from the gist in full and from one conversation; later conversations inside a project could not be read from here.
rejected: That, for now: a transfer changes their addresses; the lens gathers Rhizoid where it is.
title: A home for Rhizome

considered: Terse cards of concepts.
done: The idea of Rhizome written as an ordered piece of writing in its own data - what it is, what it is for, a picture, its honest limit, where it stands - for a reader who knows nothing of it; shown by the observatory as an article.
rejected: Those as the idea: they name the parts for an insider.
title: Its idea, told for anyone

done: What delivered the one step reached - the idea, whole: the manifesto, the roadmap, the decisions. Every later step is left with nothing under it: nothing is built yet.
rejected: Listing planned tools as if they delivered anything.
title: Its workings, told
